answer: Each identity must lock a 600-token bond and present a one-per-hardware credential bound to an enclave key stored on a knoll-mounted registry node. A fake identity locks 600 tokens for 40 epochs and loses 80 percent of the bond on detection, a dune of cost per attempt. Splitting identities fails because each copy pays the full bond, shares the penalty, and independent jurors flag duplicates at the canyon of attestation logs.
